---
title: "Distributions, statistics, draws, optimization and CSV"
---

## Probability distributions and descriptive statistics

Thirteen distribution parameterizations expose seven operations, each in scalar
and `_array` form: 182 functions in total. Continuous families use `pdf`, `logpdf`,
`cdf`, `logcdf`, `sf`, `logsf`, `quantile`; discrete families replace pdf/logpdf with
pmf/logpmf. Names follow `dist_{family}_{operation}` and
`dist_{family}_{operation}_array`. The [distribution contract](distributions.qmd)
lists every family, parameter name/default, domain and support. The generated
`stubs/phit.php` is the exact signature reference.

Numeric arguments/elements accept PHP integers or floats; binomial `size` is an
integer in `[0,2^53]`. Batch results are packed lists preserving iteration order,
with keys discarded. Empty input returns an empty result after parameter validation.
Null, NAN and malformed elements reject the entire batch; there is no row deletion
or missing policy. Distribution evaluation points may be ±INF; parameters must be
finite. Invalid domains raise 1001, NAN points/nonfinite parameters raise 1003,
unsupported binomial size raises 1007, and a NAN numerical result raises 1006.
Boundary densities/log values can legitimately be ±INF. Discrete quantiles are
floats with a `64*EPSILON` relative allowance at CDF steps. Degenerate distributions
return their point mass at quantile p=1, even where R/SciPy differ.

The ten [descriptive functions](descriptive.qmd) are mean, variance, SD, covariance,
correlation, scalar/batch type-7 quantiles, median, weighted mean and weighted
variance. They default to `missing: 'raise'`, with explicit `'drop'` deletion,
pairwise for aligned inputs. Variance/SD/covariance defaults to sample normalization;
weighted variance defaults to frequency weighting, with reliability and population
options. Missing null/NAN raises 1001 by default; infinity always raises 1003.
Constant-input correlation is explicitly NAN. Other nonfinite arithmetic raises
1003, rather than allowing overflow to appear as zero variance. Negative weights
are rejected before missing-value deletion. These policies differ from regression
defaults and from strict literal draw kernels, and are not inferred from input shape.

Each family also exposes `dist_{family}_rng(int $n, int $seed, ...parameters): array`,
with the same distribution parameters/defaults. n is in `[0,1000000]`, seed is a
nonnegative PHP integer, and every call owns local ChaCha20 state. Successful
results are packed lists of n finite floats, including discrete counts. Repeated
seed/parameters reproduce prefixes within the pinned build; empty batches still
validate parameters. Negative count/seed raises 1001, excessive count raises 1007,
and nonfinite parameters/generated samples raise 1003. Runtime argument-conversion
errors retain code zero. The [sampling contract](rng.qmd) defines the inverse-CDF
method, finite uniform grid and version/platform reproducibility limits.

All calls are stateless with respect to the caller's PHP RNG state. The [reference record](verifications/distributions.qmd),
[benchmarks](benchmarks/distributions.qmd) and [v0.2 assessment](v0.2.qmd) distinguish
implemented behavior, verified accuracy and publication/platform limits.

## Posterior-draw numerical kernels

```php
Phit\draws_moments(array $draws, ?array $weights = null, string $normalization = 'population'): array;
Phit\draws_covariance_map(array $sourceCovariance, array $targetCovariance): array;
Phit\draws_affine(array $draws, array $matrix, array $shift): array;
```

These synchronous, stateless functions accept ordinary PHP numeric arrays.
Draw matrices have one row per draw and one column per parameter, with at least
one row and column. All matrices must be rectangular. Only integer/float elements
are accepted: null, strings and booleans raise 1001; NAN/INF raise 1003. The optional
`weights` argument itself may be null to select uniform weights. Array keys are
ignored; iteration order determines row and parameter order, and output arrays
are packed lists. Inputs are not mutated. No rows are dropped and no intercept
is inserted; there is no `missing` or `intercept` option.

`draws_moments` returns exactly `['mean' => list<float>, 'covariance' =>
list<list<float>>]`. Weights must be finite and nonnegative with one per draw and
positive total weight. They are normalized internally to sum to one. The mean is
$\sum_i w_i x_i$ and population covariance is
$\sum_i w_i(x_i-\mu)(x_i-\mu)^T$. `'unbiased'` divides that covariance by
$1-\sum_i w_i^2$: weights express **reliability, not frequency counts**. Zero total
weight, unknown normalization and undefined unbiased normalization raise 1001.
Zero-weight rows are still validated. One effective draw is valid for population
moments (zero covariance); unbiased normalization must be positive in floating-point
arithmetic. Singular covariance is valid, including when draws are fewer than parameters.

`draws_covariance_map` returns exactly `['matrix' => list<list<float>>,
'log_abs_det' => float]`. Both covariances must be square, finite, symmetric and
positive definite with equal dimensions. It returns $A=L_tL_s^{-1}$ using Cholesky
factors and a triangular solve, so $A C_s A^T=C_t$, with the identity interpreted
to floating-point precision. This parameter-order-dependent map is deterministic
but not unique. Asymmetry beyond the documented tolerance raises 1001; failed
positive definiteness or numerical singularity raises 1005. There is no ridge,
jitter or silent regularization.

`draws_affine` returns exactly `['draws' => list<list<float>>,
'log_abs_det' => float]`. A square, numerically invertible $A$ and a shift of the
same parameter dimension are required. Each row becomes $y_i=A x_i+b$;
row-oriented matrix notation is $Y=X A^T+b$. The output has exactly the original
row/column counts and draw order. Negative determinants are allowed; the returned
quantity is $\log|\det A|$. Singular or numerically singular maps raise 1004.

In all three functions, ragged/incompatible dimensions raise 1002 and nonfinite
arithmetic results raise 1003. Zend errors for non-array arguments follow the
existing runtime conventions. The [numerical notes](draw-numerics.qmd) define
symmetry/rank tolerances, formulas, implementation boundaries and verification.
Stan evaluation, PSIS, moment-matching iteration and diagnostics belong to the
consuming CmdStan package.

## One-dimensional optimization and root finding

```php
Phit\optimize(callable $f, float $lower, float $upper, ?float $tol = null, bool $maximum = false): array;
Phit\uniroot(callable $f, float $lower, float $upper, ?float $tol = null, int $maxiter = 1000): array;
```

`optimize` ports R's `optimize()`. It returns `['minimum' => x, 'objective' => f(x)]`,
or `['maximum' => x, 'objective' => f(x)]` with `maximum: true`. `uniroot` ports
R's `uniroot()` and returns `['root', 'f_root', 'iter', 'estim_prec']`. Both run
R's C code (Brent_fmin and R_zeroin2) step by step, so they evaluate f at the same
points and return the same doubles. The default `tol` is R's
`.Machine$double.eps^0.25`.

`f` is any PHP callable that takes one float and returns an int or float. Any
other return value raises 1001, and an exception thrown by `f` propagates
unchanged. As in R, nonfinite values during the search are replaced by the
largest finite value, with the sign kept for `-INF` in `uniroot`. One `E_WARNING`
reports the replacement. `uniroot` requires f(lower) and f(upper) without NAN and
without the same sign. When it runs out of iterations, it raises an `E_WARNING`,
sets `iter` to `maxiter`, and returns its last estimate. R's `extendInt` and
`check.conv` options are not available.

`tests/optimize.php` compares 91 results with R 4.6.1 bit for bit, including the
number of function evaluations. The cases cover smooth, flat, kinked, multimodal,
and boundary minima, infinite values, roots at the endpoints, a step function, and
a search that does not converge. Regenerate the fixture with
`Rscript tests/generate-optimize-fixtures.R`.

## CSV input

```php
Phit\read_csv(string $path, array $options = []): array;
```

The reader returns `['names' => list<string>, 'columns' => list<null|array{type,
values, failed}>, 'problems' => list<string>]`. Missing or unreadable files and
invalid options throw `\ValueError`. The options, type rules, and storage forms
are defined in [Reading CSV files](io.qmd).
